programme.title: Sortilegio
programme.desc: Alejandro returns home after a terrible accident to discover that he is married to Maria Jose, a poor, innocent girl who was deceived by Alejandro's brother Bruno. Bruno used Alejandro's name to marry Maria Jose, soon after he sent to kill his brother in hopes that Maria Jose would inherit Alejandro's fortune. But when Maria Jose arrives at the mansion she realizes that Bruno lied to her and used her. She is also scared when Alejandro is found alive and returns home. Doctors tell Alejandro that he suffers from memory loss but he is convinced he never met Maria Jose before and goes in search of the truth, but during this time and Maria Jose actually fall in love, while Bruno and Maura (Alejandro's ex-girlfriend) plot to break them up. Meanwhile, the brothers' mother Victoria has fallen in love with Fernando--Alejandro's best friend, so closer to his age than hers.

programme.title: Rebelde

programme.title: Offline with Jon Favreau
programme.sub-title: Offline with Jon Favreau (1 Offline Host vs. 1 Jubilee Founder)
programme.desc: Can the internet foster productive debate in the rage-bait era? Jubilee founder and CEO Jason Y. Lee joins Offline to talk about his company’s massive YouTube channel, known for its viral political debates in series like Surrounded and Middle Ground. He and Jon talk about the moral quandary of platforming people like Charlie Kirk, what young people find so captivating about these conflict-ridden videos, and why Jason views his content as chocolate covered broccoli.

programme.title: Pod Save America
programme.desc: Donald Trump hides in a catering truck and boards a secret plane to evade an Iranian security threat, leaving reporters, White House officials, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio alone aboard Air Force One to fend for themselves. Dan and Jon discuss the President's profile in courage and the rest of the latest, including a series of shocking new developments with ICE, the discourse around electability after David Crowley's unexpected primary win in Wisconsin, and Nate Silver's new midterm model, which is uncharacteristically optimistic about Democrats' chances of taking back both the House and Senate. Then, the guys bid farewell to press secretary Karoline Leavitt and debate which MAGA-world figures are most likely to replace her.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (MAGA Media’s Trump Slump)
programme.desc: Donald Trump’s poll numbers are trash — and numbers for right-wing influencers on YouTube, Twitter and elsewhere are going down the tubes, too. As the New York Times reported at the end of last month, some of the biggest names in right-wing media are experiencing massive declines in clicks and views to their content. David Pakman is the host of the David Pakman Show on YouTube – and he’s been thinking a lot about the algorithms that control what we watch, read, listen to and think about. He stopped by to talk about how right-wing media has become a victim of its own success. And in headlines, Karoline Leavitt is leaving the White House at the end of the month to spend more time with her family, U.S. inflation declined slightly last month and what’s behind Zohran Mamdani’s approval rating after eight months in office.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (Reining In The Congressional Culture of Harassment)
programme.desc: The fact that the US Congress is absolutely rotten with creeps is one of the worst-kept secrets in Washington. From former Representatives like California Democrat Eric Swalwell and Texas Republican Tony Gonzales, to sitting lawmakers like North Carolina Republican Representative Chuck Edwards – it turns out sexual misconduct is bipartisan, and so is the pushback. A bipartisan effort fronted by Florida Republican Kat Cammack and New Mexico Democrat Teresa Leger Fernandez aims to rein in the frathouse behavior of their colleagues. To discuss what’s on the table, we called up Grace Panetta, political reporter with The 19th. And in headlines, Trump blames vandals for ruining a patch of grass on the National Mall, Attorney General Todd Blanche refused to pledge that he’ll operate independently from the White House, and the Supreme Court rejected another request to throw out a jury’s 2023 finding that Trump sexually abused writer E. Jean Carroll and later defamed her.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (The Reality of Being Trapped on the USS Lincoln)
programme.desc: You may have heard about the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln — the carrier where sailors have been facing food shortages and broken toilets. They’ve gone without a traditional port call for eight and a half months, and counting. But they’re not the only vessel facing long deployments and concerning conditions. In May, the USS Gerald Ford finally returned to port in the U.S. after 11 months at sea – the longest deployment since the end of the Vietnam War. Those months away from home featured a massive fire that raged for hours onboard, and – you guessed it – plumbing problems. So to talk more about what our men and women in uniform are facing because President Donald Trump started a war of choice, we spoke with Colorado Democratic Representative Jason Crow. And in headlines, Trump delays 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports, the Ebola outbreak in Congo reaches 5,000 cases, and college students at some universities can now pay their tuition using PayPal or Venmo.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.sub-title: Lovett or Leave It (Maine Character Syndrome)
programme.desc: Iran leaves the negotiating table, voters enter the polls, and Graham Platner slides into America’s DMs, for better or for worse. Meanwhile, Tig Notaro weighs in on Lovett’s wedding, RFK Jr’s snake handling, and the dawn of Slam Pig Summer. Aparna Nancherla talks anxiety, stand-up and getting your foot in the door at WikiFeet, and we look back (in horror!) with a round of Second Thoughts.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.sub-title: Lovett or Leave It (Boo York City)
programme.desc: The Big Apple spits out a worm, Trump attacks California’s elections, and Spencer Pratt packs up his dreams of mayoral stardom. This week, Michael Urie lies down on Lovett’s couch and analyzes his feelings about Harrison Ford; Kel Cripe lays out a Pride month's worth of regulations in They/Them’s the Rules, and we put the show to rest with a nice warm cup of Second Thoughts.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.sub-title: Lovett or Leave It (Scum Like It Hot)
programme.desc: It’s Part 1 of our Lovett or Leave It Pride Show Extravaganza! This week, World Cup fans taste America and demand unlimited refills, Trump wants us to chug his Iran Kool-Aid, and D.C. bellies up to the bar for this summer’s trendiest algae cocktail. Hollywood legend Bruce Vilanch gives a gay side eye to early LGBTQ moments in film, while Myki Meeks decides which 2026 Pride Merch items should sashay away. And we taste the rainbow with a very gay round of I Don’t Care, I Lovett.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.sub-title: Lovett or Leave It (The Pride Will Continue Until Morale Improves)
programme.desc: It’s Part 2 of our Lovett or Leave It Pride Show Extravaganza! This week, Lovett celebrates Nuclear Family Month, Cats: The Jellicle Ball, and Rosie O’Donnell’s incredible facelift. Meanwhile, Ashley Ray and Brendan Scannell crown America’s Top Ally. Atsuko Okatsuka joins us as we burn our hands on Hot Takes about polyamory, bitchy gays, and forcing drag queens to do the splits, and the Second Thoughts library is open as we read Lovett to filth.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.sub-title: Lovett or Leave It (The Pool is Always Greener)
programme.desc: JD Vance treads water on Iran, D.C. swan dives into Reflecting Pool chaos, and Trump lifts a glass to his brand-new Air Force One. This week, Matt Hamilton stops by to discuss local journalism, the L.A. mayoral race, and, of course, a plague of fire rats. Ali Siddiq and Ify Nwadiwe find out if Father really does know best with a round of Would You Rather?, and we have regrets like we’ve never had them before when we share our many, many Second Thoughts.

programme.title: Kika Kim Mukbang
programme.sub-title: Korean Restaurant Feast & Purple Desserts Mukbang ASMR
programme.desc: Join us for a unique ASMR mukbang episode! First, Kika Kim and Chanderland from XO Team visit an authentic Korean restaurant to enjoy spicy chicken, samgyeopsal, sushi, rice, and more. Then, explore a sweet and colorful purple food mukbang featuring chocolates, noodles, and snacks. Relax and savor every tasty moment of this special double-feature experience!

programme.title: Kika Kim Mukbang
programme.sub-title: ASMR Rainbow Dessert Picnic Mukbang in the Car

Then, enjoy a special car picnic with XO Team’s Alisha & Elsarca, sharing sweets, fruits, sushi rolls, and sandwiches. Experience the satisfying sounds and vibrant treats in this unique and delicious episode!

Then, indulge in a rich chocolate feast with Alisha, including ice cream, cookies, cake, brownies, macarons, and more. Don’t miss this deliciously entertaining episode packed with sweet surprises!

programme.sub-title: Spicy Red Food & Korean BBQ Mukbang ASMR

Relax, enjoy, and treat yourself to your favorite food while watching this tasty episode!

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - How To Translate Animal Language | The MeatEater Podcast Ep. 838 - 12 - 838
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with naturalist, writer, and sculptor George Bumann, Brody Henderson, Phil Taylore, and Corinne Schneider. Topics discussed: George's book, Eavesdropping On Animals; Animal vocalizations; subscribe to the new Bear Grease YouTube channel; laws on game retrieval; just how pungent skunk odor really is; stay tuned for MeatEater TV's new "12 in 26" hunt series, starting with Jani's Manitoba bear episode; how absurd it is that guys called better than turkeys themselves; what various raven calls mean; how the birds gossip about everything; wolf howling and squirrel chirping translations; all the animals are talking about and know you; silence as the most important alarm that exists; The Yellowstone Summit; and more. Order George's book EAVESDROPPING ON ANIMALS here: https://www.georgebumann.com/gb/eavesdropping-on-animals/ Register for The Yellowstone Summit here: https://www.yellowstonesummit.com/

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - Conservation Wins and Losses with Senator Martin Heinrich | The MeatEater Podcast Ep. 817 - 12 - 817
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with New Mexico Senator Martin Heinrich, Ryan Callaghan, and Randall Williams. Topics discussed: Corner crossing and the Supreme Court ruling; stream access; the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, mining, and caribou; the Roadless Rule; where to develop and not develop renewables; relative bipartisan support for nuclear energy; reintroducing pronghorn back to an area of New Mexico; the breadth of the coalition that came together around keeping public lands in public hands; and more.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - Arizona Jaguars, CWD Elk, and a New One-Buck Limit for Michigan Hunters | The News Show Ep. 879 - 12 - 879
programme.desc: Steven Rinella and the MeatEater crew discuss: Steve's new baby mouse; Corner Crossing updates; the endangered jaguar hanging out in Arizona; live sonar for billfish and the end of integrity in fishing; Louisiana's National Forest land transfer; the first ever detection of CWD in Wyoming's largest elk herd; South Dakota sets an unprecedented elk hunting management plan; Michigan's major buck hunting rule changes; and more.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - Attack Of The Screw Worms | The MeatEater Podcast Ep. 835 - 12 - 835
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with Caleb Hubbard of the Hubbard Urban Entymology Lab at New Mexico State University and "Bubbly" Doug Duren. Topics discussed: Stay tuned for twice a week MeatEater Podcast drops starting in March; come to the Safari Club International 2026 Convention on Feb. 19th to see Steve and Morgan Potter; a correction on Colorado wolf recovery; sous vide rewarming for frostbite; the ins and outs of the New World screw worm; how all warm blooded critters are potential hosts; being eaten alive; Doug's Sharing the Land organization; and more. The New World Screwworm Threat Survey: https://acesnmsu.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eLjo05717Wzz1em The New World Screwworm is a serious pest threat to livestock and wildlife, and New Mexico is taking steps to stay proactive-not reactive. The survey gathers input from ranchers, producers, hunters, land stewards, and community members across New Mexico. We're studying what people know, believe, and need regarding screwworm prevention and response.

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.desc: How can we truly understand ourselves? Most of us either ignore our emotions or overthink them, turning simple feelings into complex puzzles. So how do we navigate the minefield of emotion to grow and become better? Expect to learn where self-esteem really comes from, why criticism hurts so much, where imposter syndrome comes from and how to overcome it, if hustle culture is a modern phenomenon or is this something new, why we tend to intellectualise our emotions, why we have existential crisis’ and how to navigate them, why online dating is so miserable for so many people and much more…

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.desc: Are modern gender dynamics leaving men feeling ‘castrated’? While men are often blamed for today’s social problems, far less attention is given to how shifting expectations of women and relationships may also shape male identity. What role do women play in this dynamic—and how can it be improved? Expect to learn how important it is for women to seem impressed or giddy or appreciative of their partner, how women can appear more receptive or appreciative, why men are being emasculated by women, how women can stop castrating men and much more…

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.sub-title: How to Defeat Your Stress, Anxiety & Inaction
programme.desc: If motivation can’t be trusted, what should you rely on instead? Bestselling author and top podcaster Mel Robbins explains why discipline and emotional control are the real keys to success, and how to build the mindset needed to follow through when it counts. Expect to learn why we cling to control even when we know it makes us miserable and why we focus on things we can't control, how to better deal with the judgment of others, where self-compassion comes from, how to get a grip on your anxiety and ADHD, what ""Let Them"" theory means and how to employ it, where self-compassion actually comes from and much more...

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.sub-title: The Personal Pain of Country Music
programme.desc: Odds are, your favorite country song wasn’t written by the person singing it; it was probably written by HARDY (or someone in his writing circle, maybe). So how did a Mississippi country boy become one of Nashville’s most powerful behind-the-scenes writers and producers? Expect to learn what HARDY’s philosophy for his career and life is, what most people do not understand about how the Nashville scene works, how to balance the unique tension between being a songwriter and an artist, the story of the bus crash that almost killed HARDY, how to use vulnerability and turn it into a strength and much more…

programme.title: Modern Wisdom
programme.sub-title: Uncertain About Your Relationship? You Need This…
programme.desc: How do you know if you’re with the right person — or if you're just telling yourself you are? If you’re questioning the relationship more than enjoying it, Matthew Hussey might have the clarity you need. So what does finding your person actually look like, and what signs should you pay attention to? Expect to learn how to know when it’s time to leave a relationship, the 5 questions to ask yourself if you’re unsure about your relationship, why people struggle so hard with letting others go, how women can best support their man and visa versa, how important attractiveness is to both men and women in a successful relationship, ways to learnt to be more vulnerable and much more…

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: GRAMMY-winning singer-songwriter Brandon Lake joins Joel Madden to talk balancing fame and family, using music to share his relationship with faith, and previewing his upcoming album King of Hearts. He opens up about hiring a performance/health coach for life on tour, dialing in nutrition and strength training, life on a new South Carolina farm, growing up in church and learning guitar, and the joy of community in music—from a viral onstage “Higher” moment to swapping stories about Creed and meeting Scott Stapp.

programme.title: Nick Swardson: Make Joke from Face
programme.desc: Nick Swardson delivers a stand-up special filled with outrageous stories, sharp humor, and reflections on life, fame, and misadventures.

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: Actor, comedian, and master impressionist Jay Pharoah joins Joel Madden for a candid talk about early jobs, lessons from Charlie Murphy, and finding joy in comedy. Pharoah shares stories from his time on the road, his new special Jared, and how humor became his way to connect and uplift others.

programme.title: Mae Martin: "I'm a TV"
programme.desc: Tune in for the exclusive global streaming event of Mae Martin’s I’m a TV, captured live in Los Angeles. Blending intimate indie-pop songs with witty onstage banter, Mae performs new material on the eve of the album’s release—introducing the band (Jason Couse, Sophie, Wes Maskell) and sharing stories that inspired tracks like “Say the Word,” “Try Me,” “Don’t Get Tired of Me,” and “Garbage Strike.” A confessional, funny, and heartfelt set about love, reinvention, and finding calm in the chaos.

programme.title: Artist Friendly
programme.desc: Joel Madden sits down with Sarah Barthel—singer, songwriter, and one half of platinum duo Phantogram—for a candid conversation about using art to process emotion, the band’s obsessive pursuit of a singular sound, and the lifelong creative bond between Sarah and bandmate Josh Carter. They trace Phantogram’s beginnings (from beat tapes to breakthrough), balancing romance and partnership, channeling real-life heartbreak into “When I’m Small,” coping with family loss, and gearing up for a summer tour with Deftones. Cameos of warmth (including Leroy the dog) and plenty of shop talk on writing, producing, and performing.

programme.title: Frank Turner: Live from Shamrock Rebellion
programme.desc: Recorded live at Flogging Molly’s Shamrock Rebellion festival in Las Vegas, singer-songwriter Frank Turner and his band The Sleeping Souls deliver a high-energy performance filled with punk spirit, sharp storytelling, and crowd-fueled anthems. Featuring songs like I Still Believe, 1933, Girl from the Record Shop, and Never Mind the Back Problems, this exclusive Veeps concert captures Turner’s trademark mix of rebellion, heart, and unity.

programme.title: Poppy: Live at House of Blues in Anaheim
programme.desc: Poppy performs live at House of Blues Anaheim on the second leg of her “They’re All Around Us” Tour. This concert capture features dark, industrial-tinged themes and high-intensity vocals.

programme.title: NEEDTOBREATHE: The CAVES World Tour Live from Red Rocks
programme.desc: Recorded under the open sky at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Morrison, Colorado, this concert film captures NEEDTOBREATHE at the height of The CAVES World Tour. The band delivers an expansive live set blending southern rock, gospel harmonies, and cinematic emotion. Featuring performances of “Who Am I,” “Banks,” “Fever,” and “Riding High,” the night showcases the group’s dynamic musicianship and heartfelt storytelling. $1 of each ticket supports the For Others foundation, amplifying the show’s message of hope and generosity.
